publicly_readable: The editor's introduction in full, via an Internet Archive snapshot of worldin.economist.com.
not_readable: The body text of the other articles (paywalled or not archived), including the 30th-anniversary section on ways of looking into the future.

entries.quote: Woes will sadly abound in the Arab world, as people keep flooding out of Syria and other ravaged places; Europe’s handling of the migrant crisis will remain woefully inadequate.
entries.subject: Syrian refugee outflow

entries.quote: the performance of emerging markets, including a slowing China, will be disappointing, and will hold back global growth. Partly as a result corporate profits will also disappoint.
entries.subject: Emerging-market growth and corporate profits

entries.quote: Investors will be watching for rate rises at Janet Yellen’s Federal Reserve.
entries.subject: Federal Reserve rate rises
entries.note: Implies rate rises; does not state how many.

entries.quote: Hillary Clinton will be the candidate to beat in the race for the White House.
entries.subject: US presidential election 2016

entries.quote: And Brazil’s president, Dilma Rousseff, faces a battle to resist impeachment.
entries.subject: Dilma Rousseff impeachment
entries.note: Names the fight; does not predict the outcome.

entries.quote: and cricket-crazy India will win out in the T20 World Cup in March.
entries.subject: ICC World Twenty20 2016 winner

notes: Edition number 30 stated in the introduction ('in our 30th'). The introduction also states that the first edition was The World in 1987. Publication day in November 2015 not confirmed; month only.
